# Repertoire

> Repertoire installs an agent skill into every coding agent you use and pins it
> with a lockfile you commit. A skill is a `SKILL.md` package; a catalog is a Git
> repository; the lock records the catalog commit and a content digest per
> target, so `repertoire update` refreshes the copies it owns and refuses one you
> edited by hand.

Repertoire supports 30 agent targets, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor,
GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, Windsurf and OpenCode. It installs under the home
directory by default, or into the current Git worktree with `--project`. It
stores no tokens, sends no telemetry, and works with private catalogs over the
Git credentials you already have.

## Start here

- [Home](https://phillarmonic.github.io/repertoire-ai/): what Repertoire is, the update refusal as a transcript, install on Windows, Linux, macOS or from source, and five minutes to a first lock.
- [The skill lockfile](https://phillarmonic.github.io/repertoire-ai/concepts/lockfile/): what `repertoire.lock.json` records, exactly what the content digest covers, and why an update refuses an edited copy.
- [Repertoire vs copy-paste](https://phillarmonic.github.io/repertoire-ai/vs-copy-paste/): the comparison against copying folders and against a shared skills repository, including when copying is the better answer.

## Guides

- [Set up a project or team](https://phillarmonic.github.io/repertoire-ai/automation/): commit a manifest, then bootstrap the same skills on a new machine or in CI.
- [Let your agent drive Repertoire](https://phillarmonic.github.io/repertoire-ai/agent-skill/): the built-in `repertoire` skill, which lets a coding agent install skills, write manifests and scaffold catalogs.
- [Private and company catalogs](https://phillarmonic.github.io/repertoire-ai/private-repositories/): publish skills from a private Git repository, with loose catalogs and overrides.
- [Troubleshooting](https://phillarmonic.github.io/repertoire-ai/troubleshooting/): what each error message means, and what `repertoire doctor` checks.

## Reference

- [Command reference](https://phillarmonic.github.io/repertoire-ai/commands/): every command, flag and edge case.
- [Manifests and state](https://phillarmonic.github.io/repertoire-ai/concepts/manifests/): `repertoire.yaml`, the lock file, and how declared state differs from installed state.
- [Catalogs](https://phillarmonic.github.io/repertoire-ai/concepts/catalogs/): catalog layout, loose catalogs, and source-qualified skill IDs.
- [Targets and security](https://phillarmonic.github.io/repertoire-ai/concepts/targets-security/): the 30 target directories, trust blocks, signed commits and digest signatures.
- [Glossary](https://phillarmonic.github.io/repertoire-ai/glossary/): skill, catalog, lock file, managed copy, provenance and the other terms in one place.

## Project

- [GitHub](https://github.com/phillarmonic/repertoire-ai): source, releases and issues.
- [Contributing](https://phillarmonic.github.io/repertoire-ai/contributing/): build and test Repertoire itself.
